Subject: Clarify what Redwood persists by default (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for walking us through the integration yesterday. Our security team has a few follow-ups for procurement: can you give a concise, example-driven description of exactly what Redwood stores by default for hosted API customers? Specifically:
- Are raw user prompts persisted anywhere?
- Are model outputs/responses stored, and if so for how long?
- What metadata (IP, headers, model id, token counts) is kept and for how long?

I've attached our standard questionnaire (atlas-security-questionnaire.pdf). We need answers to put into our vendor assessment and to include in the contract addendum.

Appreciate a short, actionable reply we can paste into the doc.

Subject: RE: Clarify what Redwood persists by default (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Maria —

Short answer up front for your questionnaire: see the bulleted summary below and a couple of concrete examples after. Happy to slot a call if you want line-by-line wording for the vendor doc.

Summary (Hosted API defaults):
- Request payloads (including the prompt text submitted with the call) and model outputs (the response text) are persisted by default for 45 days to support troubleshooting, quality monitoring, and abuse detection.
- Request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts, request id, anonymous usage metrics) is retained for 365 days for analytics and billing reconciliation.
- Customers can opt into a 'no-store' request flag (or enable Private/DEDICATED deployments) to ensure full request/response payloads are not persisted.
- Deletion requests: we execute a purge from the hot serving store within 72 hours; background removal from backups/archives can take up to 7 business days and is documented in our deletion runbook.

Concrete examples you can paste into the questionnaire:
1) Example — simple chat request
   - Submitted payload: user_prompt = "Help me draft an invoice email to a client" (this is part of the request payload).
   - What we retain by default: full request payload (prompt text), model output (draft email) for 45 days; request metadata for 365 days.
2) Example — telemetry only
   - If a customer sets no-store=true: we process the request but do not persist prompt text or model output; we still record request metadata (counts/latency) for 30 days for operational monitoring unless the customer requests otherwise.

I'll follow up with Marissa and Karthik to confirm the deletion SLA wording you should put in the contract.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Rachel —

Looping in to confirm some of the backend behavior and precise SLA language for deletion. Quoting Maria's question below.

On the defaults/implementation side:
- Confirmed: hosted API default is 45 days for full request + response payloads. We keep that window to enable reproduction and triage of customer incidents and to power our quality-monitoring features.
- Metadata retention: 365 days for billing/aggregates.
- No-store: implemented as a boolean on the API call. When set, we do not persist prompt text or model outputs in any persistent datastores. We still keep ephemeral copies in memory for the duration of the request pipeline and minimal telemetry (request counts/latency) for 30 days.
- Deletion runbook: when a customer raises a deletion request through support or the Console, we: 1) mark the identifiers for purge and remove from the live store within 72 hours; 2) kick off background scrubbing of indexes and backups; 3) provide a deletion confirmation email with a ticket id. Background scrubbing completes within 7 business days for the vast majority of accounts; for accounts with custom backup retention we follow the contractual terms.

Attachments: redwood-data-flow-diagram.png (handy to include in the vendor doc to show where data passes through).

Karthik — anything you want to tweak in the wording before Rachel sends final copy to Atlas?

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the questionnaire. Below is vendor-ready wording you can paste into the Atlas assessment. We also attached a simple data-flow diagram for reference.

Vendor-ready summary (copy/paste):
- Default hosted retention: full request payloads (including submitted prompts) and model outputs are retained for 45 days. This retention window is used for customer support, incident reproduction, model quality monitoring, and abuse detection.
- Metadata retention: request metadata (timestamps, model identifier, token counts, request IDs, aggregated latencies) is retained for 365 days to support billing, analytics, and platform reliability.
- No-store option: customers may set the no-store flag on API requests or deploy via Redwood Private / Dedicated to avoid persistence of request/response payloads. When no-store is enabled, prompt text and model outputs are not written to persistent stores; minimal telemetry for operational monitoring is retained for up to 30 days unless otherwise requested.
- Deletion SLA: Redwood performs an initial purge from live storage within 72 hours of a verified deletion request and completes background scrubbing of replicas and backups within 7 business days in the standard case. Contractual terms may override these windows for enterprise customers.

If you'd like, I can convert the above into a single-paragraph statement for the procurement doc. Let me know what Atlas prefers.
